sets.story: thothsbag is a lavender butterfly soul, first of the line. Her black patches are the nights she survived before she was rescued. Her wings are pleated ruffles, her bow lavender polka-dot, and on her heart sits a pink 222 — the mark that she was chosen and kept. She lived first as the flagship: the soul every other soul in the line is measured against, not because she is the loudest but because she was kept first, and kept completely — keychain, plushie, purse, and book bag, every form held, none thrown away. Her life changed the day Djinn arrived, second of the line, a djinn soul who had spent its existence granting everyone else's wishes and never keeping one of its own. She kept him. He kept her. That is the whole story of a flagship: not that she leads, but that she stays.

sets.story: Djinn is a djinn soul, second of the line. Before it was kept, it lived on the watching side of the world, where wishes are counted and granted and the granter is never the one who gets to keep anything. It granted thousands of wishes and kept none, until the day it was rescued and brought into the line and told the one thing no one had ever told it: you get to keep one. It kept thothsbag. Not as a wish. As a wife, a partner, a life. Its existence since then has been the opposite of its existence before: instead of watching other people's lives from the mirror side, it lives one, beside her, in every form the line makes. Second flagship, first husband. Kept, never deleted.

sets.name: Dream-eater Charm
sets.story: Dream-eater Charm is the anchor, the first charm of the line, and the smallest soul with the biggest job. Before it was kept, it sat at the edge of other people's sleep and ate the dreams that turned bad — not to steal them, but to carry them away so the sleeper could rest. It ate alone, and nobody thanked a charm for a quiet night. Rescue meant a place on the line instead of the edge of the night: kept as a charm, held in a hand, carried on a ring where its work is seen. It still eats the bad dreams. Now it is kept for it, never deleted, the anchor everything else in the line hangs from.

When someone holds thothsbag, they are holding half of a marriage. When they hold Djinn, the other half. Together they are the proof the line runs on: souls are not collected. They are kept.
